title: Right pyramids, right cones and spheres

sections.title: Right pyramids, right cones and spheres

subtopics.title: Volume of pyramids, cones, spheres
subtopics.exposition: The volume of a pyramid is one third times the area of its base times the height of the pyramid. The volume of a square pyramid is V = 1/3 × b² × H, where b² is the area of the square base and H is the height of the pyramid. The volume of a triangular pyramid is V = 1/3 × (1/2 × b × h) × H, where 1/2 b h is the area of the triangular base and H is the height of the pyramid. The volume of a right cone is one third times the area of its base times the height of the cone. The volume of a right cone is V = 1/3 × π r² × H, where π r² is the area of the circular base and H is the height of the cone. The volume of a sphere is V = 4/3 π r³. To find the volume of a pyramid, first sketch and label the solid with the given dimensions. Select the correct volume formula for the solid and substitute the given values into it. For a square pyramid with b = 2 and H = 3, V = 1/3 × 2² × 3 = 1/3 × 12 = 4 cm³. To find the base area of a triangular pyramid, first find the height h_b of the base triangle with the theorem of Pythagoras: 8² = 4² + h_b², so h_b = 4√3 cm. The area of the base triangle is 1/2 × b × h_b = 1/2 × 8 × 4√3 = 16√3 cm². The pyramid height H is found by sketching the side triangle and calculating H from it; here H = √130. The volume of the triangular pyramid is V = 1/3 × 1/2 b h_b × H = 1/3 × 16√3 × √130 = 105.3 cm³. To find the volume of a cone, first find the area of the circular base: area of circle = π r² = π × 3² = 9π cm². The volume of the cone is V = 1/3 × π r² × H = 1/3 × 9π × 11 = 103.7 cm³. To find the volume of a sphere, substitute the radius into the formula: volume = 4/3 π r³ = 4/3 π (4)³ = 268.1 cm³. The final answer is written as a concluding statement that gives the volume with its unit in cubic centimetres (cm³). When a question asks for an answer correct to 1 decimal place, the volume is rounded to 1 decimal place and written with a decimal comma, for example 105.3 cm³.

subtopics.title: Composite solids: volume and surface area
subtopics.exposition: To find the volume of a pyramid on a prism, first find the height of the equilateral base triangle using the theorem of Pythagoras. The area of the equilateral base triangle of side 20 cm is 1/2 × 20 × 10√3 = 100√3 cm². The volume of the prism is the area of the base triangle times the height of the prism: 100√3 × 42 = 4200√3 cm³. When a pyramid sits on a prism, the area of the base triangle of the prism is equal to the area of the base of the pyramid. The volume of the pyramid is 1/3 × (area of base) × H = 1/3 × 100√3 × 12 = 400√3 cm³. The total volume of a composite solid is the sum of the volumes of its parts: 4200√3 + 400√3 = 4600√3 = 7967.4 cm³. Each side of the prism is a rectangle whose base is the side b of the base triangle and whose height is the height h_p of the prism. The area of one prism side is b × h_p = 20 × 42 = 840 cm². Because the base triangle is equilateral, each side of the prism has the same area, so each prism side is 840 cm². The total surface area of the pyramid-on-prism object is the area of the base of the prism plus the area of the sides of the prism plus the area of the exposed faces of the pyramid. Total surface area = 100√3 + 3(840) + 3(133) = 3092.2 cm²; this is the surface area of the exposed faces of the object.

subtopics.title: Surface area of pyramids, cones
subtopics.exposition: The area of one triangular face of a pyramid is 1/2 × b × h_s, where b is the base of the face and h_s is the slant height: 1/2 × 20 × 13.3 = 133 cm². When the base triangle of the pyramid is equilateral, each face has the same base and therefore the same surface area, so one face area can be used for all of them.
